Name of the ioBroker project or installa: Name of the ioBroker project or installation. Shown in exports and notifications. Example: Demo home or Musterhaus Schulweg (use fictional labels in public screenshots).
Target audience for the generated docume: Target audience for the generated documentation
Headings, labels, and fixed wording in A: Headings, labels, and fixed wording in Admin, User/Family, and Onboarding HTML exports and in Markdown follow this language (English / German / French). Adapter names, state ids, and room strings from ioBroker stay unchanged.
Markdown export and default documentatio:
Markdown export and default documentation focus follow this choice.

Every run still generates all three HTML profiles (admin, user, onboarding). User/Onboarding AI runs when an AI provider is configured — not controlled by this dropdown.
Short description of what should be docu: Short description of what should be documented
What the installation covers in one or t:
What the installation covers in one or two sentences (e.g. family home: heating, lighting, security). Shown in exports as the short system summary.

Counts toward the optional documentation setup score when that check is on (Advanced tab — minimum length).
Optional notes, devices, adapters or spe: Optional notes, devices, adapters or special requirements
If enabled, documentation is queued each: If enabled, documentation is queued each time the adapter starts (runs in the background; the instance can show green before it finishes). If disabled, a run still happens once after an update when the built-in HTML renderer version no longer matches info.templateVersion. Check the log for "Documentation generated via startup" and state info.lastTrigger.
If enabled, documentation regenerates wh: If enabled, documentation regenerates when adapters are installed, removed, or enabled or disabled. 30 s debounce groups bursts of changes into one run after a short quiet period.
If enabled, current values for selected: If enabled, current values for selected state roles are read and shown in User/Onboarding room cards and the Admin device table (badges next to device names). Includes e.g. temperature, blinds (level.blind), dimmers, lights (switch.light), outlets (switch/plug), humidity, power metrics, locks, door/window/contact, motion, alarm. Room members may be channels or devices — matching child states are found automatically. Very custom or empty roles are skipped.
Optional timer: regenerate every X hours: Optional timer: regenerate every X hours, independent of start and adapter-change options above. 0 = no scheduled runs (events and start still work). Example: 24 = about once per day.
When enabled, disabled adapter instances: When enabled, disabled adapter instances are omitted from instance lists in every export (HTML and Markdown).
When enabled, Markdown skips per-instanc: When enabled, Markdown skips per-instance detail blocks and keeps overview-style sections. HTML exports still list instances as usual.
Hide “changes since last run” in Admin e: Hide “changes since last run” in Admin exports
When enabled, the yellow delta box at th: When enabled, the yellow delta box at the top of the Admin HTML System overview and the matching subsection in Admin Markdown are omitted. Changelog history is unchanged; User and Onboarding exports are unchanged.
After the optional enabled-only filter,: After the optional enabled-only filter, only the first N instances in discovery order are kept (0 = unlimited). Applies to HTML and Markdown.
Used for the info.htmlUrl state and book: Used for the info.htmlUrl state and bookmark/QR targets. Include host and port, e.g. http://192.168.1.100:8081 or https://iobroker.home:443 — no trailing slash. Protocol is optional. Leave empty for auto-detection (may fail in Docker).
How many timestamped file sets to keep (: How many timestamped file sets to keep (per type: .md, .html, .json). Oldest are deleted automatically. 0 = use default (3).
Advanced documentation storage hint:
Full Markdown, the JSON model, and Admin HTML are always stored under this adapter's Files (`autodoc-latest.md`, `autodoc-latest.json`, `autodoc-admin.html`, plus profile HTML). The states `documentation.markdown`, `documentation.html`, and `documentation.json` hold short placeholders only so the object database stays small.

Use `info.htmlUrl*` and `/files/` for full text, or the download actions (they copy from the latest files). `documentation.exportHashes` still lists SHA-256 digests for change detection (and PDF filenames after a successful PDF export).
Additional manual information to include: Additional manual information to include in documentation (description, contact, notes)
Admin tab orientation AI: Optional: connect an AI provider to add short explanations in exports. Leave the provider on Disabled unless you want this. Local Ollama keeps data on your network; cloud providers send metadata and text to external servers — see the privacy note below.
Admin tab orientation basic:
You are on Basic settings: language, when documentation regenerates, optional live values in room cards, Generate now / last run / forum card.

My documentation, Advanced, and HTML export & extra sections hold the main texts and options; Notifications and AI documentation (at the end) are optional.
Admin tab orientation documentation:
This tab is the reader-facing text in your exports.

Advanced: filters, Markdown detail limits, ioBroker base URL (bookmark & QR targets), where large exports live (Files + short state placeholders — see hint on Advanced), optional filesystem copy, optional PDF after each run, documentation setup score.

HTML export & extra sections: theme, chapter visibility/order, custom Markdown sections — the PDF checkbox stays on Advanced (short reminder at the top of the HTML tab).

AI context hints are prompt-only (never exported); they appear under AI documentation once a provider is enabled.
Admin tab orientation notify: Optional: send a message (e.g. Telegram, email) after each documentation run. Skip this tab if you do not need alerts.
Advanced styling open hint:
Optional expert settings: change the font or add CSS on top of the theme preset and color scheme above. Leave empty to keep the default look. A syntax error in CSS can break the layout.

Chapter visibility and custom Markdown sections are in the blocks above on this tab — not part of this section.
Advanced setup score intro:
Optional checklist in the Admin export only — it never blocks generation.

Toggle the rows below and tune limits (project description length, base URL, unassigned instances) to fit how you maintain documentation.
Maintenance score description check help: If on, Project description (My documentation tab) shorter than the minimum below is marked Needs attention in the Admin export checklist. Turn off if you like it short.
Maintenance score base URL check help: When enabled, the setup score requires a non-empty ioBroker base URL above (QR codes, bookmark links, troubleshooting bookmarks).
Maintenance score unassigned check help: When enabled, the setup score fails when the number of enabled adapter instances not assigned to any room is ≥ the threshold below. Many setups skip rooms on purpose — raise the threshold or disable this check.
Maintenance score min description length: Trimmed characters; used only when the description check above is on. Default 40; adapter clamps to 5–2000.
Maintenance score unassigned warn at hel: Shows Needs attention when unassigned count is ≥ this. Default 10; adapter clamps to 1–500. Lower = stricter. Many installs leave infra adapters unroomed — set above your usual baseline.
Admin export scripts hint: In the generated Admin HTML/Markdown, JavaScript scripts are listed by ioBroker folder (Global first, with a short reminder). This matches the Script Engine tree — not a separate AutoDoc setting.
Manual documentation hint: These fields are shown in all documentation profiles. Use “Help & emergencies”, “Routines (your words)”, and “How we run this home (your playbook)” for guests and family in plain language — nothing is invented automatically. Optional Mermaid diagram: flowcharts or similar you write yourself; optional auto host topology (instances per ioBroker host, node-capped). Hide the manual diagram with id `mermaid`, the auto diagram with `mermaidAuto`. In HTML, diagrams can be embedded as SVG during export when `@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` is installed on the host (see each field’s help); otherwise the browser loads Mermaid from the network. Adapter and room notes make the documentation more readable for non-technical users. In the Admin HTML/Markdown export, JavaScript scripts are grouped by ioBroker folder; see the short note under “Global scripts” about execution order and sensible use.
Who to call, what to try if something fa: Who to call, what to try if something fails, where the fuse box is — your words only; nothing is invented automatically.
Describe in everyday language what often: Describe in everyday language what often runs by itself (lights, heating, blinds). Shown near the script list; complements technical script names.
Optional diagram you write (flowchart, s:
Optional diagram you write (flowchart, sequence, …). HTML: with `@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` on the ioBroker host, diagrams render to embedded SVG during export (offline-friendly `file://`). Without the CLI: `<pre class="mermaid">` loads Mermaid 10.9.1 from jsDelivr when viewed online; jsDelivr is omitted once everything is SVG.

Markdown uses a ```mermaid fence (not pre-rendered). User/Onboarding hide id `mermaid` hides this diagram (`mermaidAuto` is only for the auto-host diagram below). Very long input is truncated. Tip: `flowchart LR` uses horizontal width; `flowchart TB` stacks vertically.
When enabled, adds a second HTML diagram: When enabled, adds a second HTML diagram: adapter instances grouped by ioBroker host (multihost). Instance nodes are capped (next setting); not a full wiring graph. Hide lists: `mermaidAuto` hides only this auto diagram; `mermaid` hides your manual diagram above. Same SVG/jsDelivr embedding as manual Mermaid.
Max instances in auto topology diagram: Max instances in auto topology diagram
Maximum adapter instance nodes in the au: Maximum adapter instance nodes in the auto-generated diagram (8–200, default 40). Hosts are still shown; instances are chosen round-robin across hosts when there are more than this limit.
Troubleshooting quick lines hint: Short one-liners for guests and family (Wi‑Fi, power, water, other). They appear in the Help & emergencies block together with bookmark links to this documentation (same URLs as QR codes — requires Base URL under Advanced). All optional; nothing is invented automatically.
One line, e.g. guest Wi-Fi name or where: One line, e.g. guest Wi-Fi name or where a repeater is — optional.
One line, e.g. where the electrical pane: One line, e.g. where the electrical panel is — optional.
One line, e.g. where to turn off main wa: One line, e.g. where to turn off main water — optional.
One more short line (alarm code location: One more short line (alarm code location, key box, etc.) — optional.
Who manages this system? e.g. 'Max Muste: Who manages this system? e.g. 'Max Mustermann, Telegram @max' - shown so guests and family know who to ask
General notes about this installation (e: General notes about this installation (e.g. special setups, known issues)
Anything that doesn't fit elsewhere: e.g: Anything that doesn't fit elsewhere: e.g. 'Backup runs every Sunday, server is in the basement' — same field for maintenance windows, NAS paths, or hardware quirks.
Add a human-readable note for specific a: Add a human-readable note for specific adapters (shown in all profiles). Table row example: adapter hue — note Living room scenes — wall switch overrides.
Add a human-readable note for specific r: Add a human-readable note for specific rooms (shown in User and Onboarding profiles). Example: room Kitchen — note Gas shutoff — left of sink.
Generate now hint: Click the button below to generate the documentation immediately without restarting the adapter. All three profiles (Admin, User, Onboarding) are generated simultaneously.
Start documentation generation now? This: Start documentation generation now? This may take a few seconds.
Sends sanitized script source to the sam: Sends sanitized script source to the same AI provider to add short plain-language explanations in User/Onboarding docs. Lines matching common secret patterns are redacted first; still review before enabling on production systems.
Max characters of script source per KI c: Max characters of script source per KI call
How many characters of each script (afte: How many characters of each script (after redaction) are sent to the model; longer sources are truncated. Default 12000. Lower to speed up or fit small context; raise only if your model and timeout allow. Range 2000–100000. State info.aiScriptSourceProgress shows e.g. 5/12 while processing.
Cancel script KI hint: Use this if a long script-AI run must be stopped: set action.cancelScriptSourceAi, use the button, or sendTo command cancelScriptSourceAi. The current KI request may still finish; further scripts are skipped. info.aiScriptSourceProgress shows cancelled when the phase ends.
Stop the optional per-script KI pass? Th: Stop the optional per-script KI pass? The request that is already running may still finish; further scripts will not be started. (The main user/onboarding KI calls run before this phase.)
User hide hint: Rooms and adapters in the tables below are hidden in the User/Family profile (Rooms chapter, device lists, Quick Start where they appear). Admin documentation is unchanged.
User hidden rooms help: Exact room label as in Admin → Rooms; spelling and case must match—typos or alternate wording hide nothing.
User hidden adapters help: Adapter name without instance (e.g. hue, not hue.0). One line per adapter; every hue.* instance is hidden in this profile.
Onboarding hide hint: Rooms and adapters in the tables below are hidden in the Onboarding (guest) profile — handy for technical areas (server, backup) guests do not need. Admin and User/Family exports are unchanged.
Onboarding hidden rooms help: Exact room label as in Admin → Rooms (e.g. Server room, Backup). Spelling and case must match—otherwise nothing is hidden.
Onboarding hidden adapters help: Without instance number (e.g. backitup, simple-api). Each line hides all instances of that adapter in guest listings.
Onboarding guest view — list internal Ja: Onboarding guest view — list internal JavaScript file names
onboarding guest script names help: Off (default): guest Onboarding shows only how many JavaScript automations are active — no internal script file names, and no per-script lines in Quick Start (ioBroker common.desc is not a reliable guest-facing “description”). On: legacy — up to five script names in “What runs automatically?” plus a short “more running” line; Quick Start may still list scripts with name + common.desc as today. Full detail stays in the Admin profile.
Legacy JSON field. Use the 'My documenta: Legacy JSON field. Use the 'My documentation' tab instead. Only needed for migration.
If enabled, the messaging instance below: If enabled, the messaging instance below sends a message after each successful documentation run (manual Generate or the same automatic triggers as generation).
Adapter instance that delivers the notif: Adapter instance that delivers the notification, e.g. telegram.0 or pushover.0. Must be installed and enabled in ioBroker; use the exact instance id from Objects / Instances.
Telegram username, Pushover device, or e: Telegram username, Pushover device, or email address - leave empty for adapter default. Examples: Telegram @nickname, email ops@example.com, Pushover device phone.
Use {project}, {summary}, {version}, {tr: Use {project}, {summary}, {version}, {trigger} as placeholders. Leave empty for default message. Example: {project} — documentation updated ({trigger}). {summary}
Select an AI provider for narrative summ: Select an AI provider for narrative summaries. Not used for admin profile (all data is already factual).
AI privacy warning: ⚠️ Privacy note: Cloud providers (Mistral, Groq, Anthropic) receive adapter names, room names, JavaScript script titles, and optional script purpose text (common.desc) when present. No passwords or IP addresses are sent, but your smart home structure is visible to the provider. Ollama runs locally — nothing leaves your network.
AI hardware hint: ℹ️ Low-power hosts (e.g. Raspberry Pi) or CPU-only Ollama: small models run faster but summaries may be rougher or less reliable — that is expected. You can disable AI here; Markdown/HTML docs still generate from your real ioBroker data. For better text: run Ollama on a faster PC/NAS and set the Ollama base URL to that host, or use a cloud provider if the privacy trade-off is acceptable.
Groq — US, free tier (data may be used f: Groq — US, free tier (data may be used for training)
Anthropic Claude — paid, no training on: Anthropic Claude — paid, no training on data
Ollama recommended: runs locally, no dat: Ollama recommended: runs locally, no data leaves your network. Cloud providers send adapter and room identifiers, script titles, and any optional common.desc text to external servers.
Leave empty for default. Ollama: llama3.2 / gemma3. Mistral: mistral-small-latest. Groq: llama-3.3-70b-versatile. Anthropic: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001
Mistral: console.mistral.ai | Groq: star: Mistral: console.mistral.ai | Groq: starts with gsk_... | Anthropic: starts with sk-ant-... | Ollama: leave empty
Maximum wait for one LLM HTTP request. D: Maximum wait for one LLM HTTP request. Default 300. Each generation uses several calls (user, onboarding, sometimes a German polish pass). Increase for slow local models on CPU (e.g. 480 or 600 for llama3.1:8b on NAS). Range 30–900.
Sampling temperature for resident-facing: Sampling temperature for resident-facing AI text. Leave empty for the provider default. Typical range 0–2 (Ollama, Groq, Mistral); Anthropic accepts 0–1 (values above 1 are clamped). Lower ≈ steadier wording; higher ≈ more variation — tune after testing.
Sampling temperature for guest/onboardin: Sampling temperature for guest/onboarding AI text. Same rules as user profile. The German Sie polish pass uses a fixed low temperature and ignores this field.
Export path hint: Optional: additional export to a real filesystem path outside ioBroker's database. Leave empty to disable. Examples: /mnt/nas/autodoc, D:Docssmarthome. All three profiles (admin/user/onboarding) are written as HTML files. When PDF export is enabled and puppeteer is installed in this adapter folder, matching autodoc-*.pdf files are mirrored here too. Useful for accessing the documentation when ioBroker is down, or for serving via a web server.
Pdf export after generation label: Generate PDF after each documentation run
Pdf export after generation help: Optional: after each successful run, write autodoc-admin.pdf, autodoc-user.pdf, autodoc-onboarding.pdf via headless Chromium (`puppeteer` in this adapter folder). Same sandbox flags as Mermaid CLI. Embedded SVG prints offline; jsDelivr Mermaid needs internet during PDF. Large docs: minutes and noticeable RAM/CPU. Manual trigger: state action.exportPdf (no full regeneration).
AI context hints hint:
Private to the AI — never appears in exported docs. Use short bullets with concrete facts (rooms, times, routines); vague filler does not help the model.

Guest / onboarding: Everyday language. Heavy admin or IT jargon may force neutral boilerplate for visitors instead of raw AI output (on purpose). User/family profile is not filtered the same way.

Examples: `- Living-room lights off at 22:30` · `- Guest Wi‑Fi label on the router`
AI context hints help: Prompt-only — not copied into HTML/Markdown exports. Sent to your AI provider each run. Guest profile: dense admin/IT wording here may yield neutral boilerplate for visitors (see grey box). Prefer plain facts, e.g. `- Bedroom blinds close at 22:00`.
Doc layout intro:
HTML (admin, user, onboarding): theme & logo at the top, chapter visibility and custom sections next, optional font / extra CSS at the bottom.

Hide lists and chapter order also apply to Markdown when you pick the same documentation profile on the Basic tab.
Doc layout pdf hint:
PDF: under Advanced (below disk export). Optional after each run, or anytime via `action.exportPdf`.

Requires `puppeteer` in this adapter folder; writes `autodoc-*.pdf` to Files (and mirrors to your path if set).
Advanced HTML styling hint: Expert / optional: Custom font and CSS change how exported HTML looks. Syntax mistakes or future AutoDoc updates can make the layout look wrong — leave these fields empty if you are unsure.
HTML color scheme help: Auto: visitors can toggle light/dark; preference is stored in the browser. Light / Dark: fixed look; the toggle is hidden. Does not affect Markdown files.
HTML theme preset help: Adjusts the built-in CSS variable palette (background, text, links, table headers, …) for exported HTML only. Lighter on writing custom CSS: change the preset first, use Extra CSS only for fine-tuning. Works with the color scheme above (light and dark each get a matching palette).
Sidebar logo URL help: Optional image above the search box in exported HTML. Use https://… or a same-site path starting with / — e.g. `/files/autodoc.0/logo.png` after you upload a logo to Files. Other schemes are ignored.
Font stack help:
Optional `font-family` value for body text, e.g. `Georgia, serif` or `system-ui, sans-serif`. Characters `< > { }` are stripped for safety.

Example paste: `"Source Serif 4", Georgia, serif` — quotation marks help multi-word family names.
Admin chapter order hint: Optional: reorder Admin HTML and Admin Markdown. Enter chapter ids in the JSON field below (`[]` = built-in order). Ids you omit are appended in the default product order at the end. The full list of valid English ids appears only in that field’s help (click the `?` tooltip) — it is not repeated here.
Admin chapter order JSON help: JSON array of chapter ids, e.g. `["system","adapters","manual"]`. Valid ids (exact English): `manual`, `system`, `adapters`, `rooms`, `scripts`, `schedule`, `userdata`, `aliases`, `maintenance`, `diagnosis`, `troubleshooting`, `custom`, `changelog`, `appendices`. Unknown ids are skipped; omitted ids append in default order. `[]` = built-in order.
Admin hidden chapters hint: Chapter ids to omit from Admin HTML and from Markdown when the profile is Admin — e.g. `["diagnosis","changelog","custom"]`. Same valid English ids as for chapter order; the full list is only in the help for Admin chapter order (that JSON field is below on this page). Invalid ids are ignored.
Admin hidden chapters JSON help: JSON array, e.g. `["userdata","aliases"]`. Same valid ids as Admin chapter order (see that field). `[]` = show all chapters.
Custom sections JSON hint: JSON array of objects: `{ "title": "Wi-Fi", "body": "Guest …", "profiles": ["user","onboarding"] }`. body is Markdown (no raw HTML). profiles optional — omit to show in all three HTML profiles. Max 12 sections; long text is truncated. Example uses: emergency contacts, Wi-Fi, router model.
Custom sections JSON help: See the hint above. Run Generate documentation again after edits.
User hidden chapters hint: JSON array of chapter ids to hide in User/Family HTML and in Markdown when the documentation profile is User. Example: `["scripts","adapters"]`. Valid ids: `manual`, `ai`, `guestHelp`, `atAGlance`, `rooms`, `scripts`, `routines`, `ownerPlaybook`, `mermaid` (user-defined Mermaid diagram), `mermaidAuto` (auto-generated host topology — not shown in Onboarding), `adapters`, `custom`, `system`, `troubleshooting`.
User hidden chapters JSON help: JSON array, e.g. `["scripts","adapters"]`. Invalid ids are ignored. `[]` = show all.
User chapter order hint: Optional: reorder User/Family HTML and User Markdown chapters. Enter chapter ids below in the desired order. Valid ids: `manual`, `ai`, `guestHelp`, `atAGlance`, `rooms`, `scripts`, `routines`, `ownerPlaybook`, `mermaid`, `adapters`, `custom`, `system`, `troubleshooting` — any id you omit is appended in the default order. Empty `[]` = default order. `atAGlance` appears only when the structured Quick Start block has data (discovery); reordering cannot create that content.
User chapter order JSON help: JSON array of chapter ids, e.g. `["atAGlance","rooms","manual","adapters"]`. Valid ids: `manual`, `ai`, `guestHelp`, `atAGlance`, `rooms`, `scripts`, `routines`, `ownerPlaybook`, `mermaid`, `adapters`, `custom`, `system`, `troubleshooting`. Unknown ids skipped; omitted ids append in default order. `[]` = built-in order. `atAGlance` outputs only when Quick Start has content.
Onboarding hidden chapters hint: Hide blocks in Onboarding HTML and matching parts of Markdown (profile Onboarding). Valid ids: `welcome`, `tips`, `guestHelp`, `stats`, `ai`, `capabilities`, `mermaid` (owner diagram in the welcome area), `rooms`, `routines`, `ownerPlaybook`, `automations`, `adapters`, `custom`, `hint`, plus for Markdown also `quickstart`, `system`, `manual` (project description/contact in welcome + manual chapter subsections).
Onboarding hidden chapters JSON help: JSON array, e.g. `["adapters","stats"]`. Invalid ids are ignored. `[]` = show all.
Onboarding chapter order hint:
Optional: reorder Onboarding/Guest HTML and Onboarding Markdown chapters.

Valid ids: `welcome`, `quickstart`, `tips`, `guestHelp`, `stats`, `ai`, `capabilities`, `mermaid`, `rooms`, `routines`, `ownerPlaybook`, `automations`, `adapters`, `custom`, `hint`, `system`, `manual` — any id you omit is appended in the default order.

Empty `[]` = default order.

`quickstart` always includes the welcome line, adapter counts, and next steps; the discovery snapshot (rooms / setup lines from your installation) appears only when that data exists.
Onboarding chapter order JSON help: JSON array of chapter ids, e.g. `["quickstart","tips","rooms","adapters"]`. Valid ids: `welcome`, `quickstart`, `tips`, `guestHelp`, `stats`, `ai`, `capabilities`, `mermaid`, `rooms`, `routines`, `ownerPlaybook`, `automations`, `adapters`, `custom`, `hint`, `system`, `manual`. Unknown ids skipped; omitted ids append in default order. `[]` = built-in order. `quickstart` always shows welcome, counts, next steps; discovery block only when `quickStart.hasContent`.
Advanced base URL callout: Guests & QR / copy link: Enter the URL you would use in a phone browser to open ioBroker Admin (scheme + host + port, no trailing slash). If that differs from Docker-internal hostnames or from a reverse-proxy public name, set it explicitly — auto-detection often fails in containers or behind HTTPS offload.
